113.tasks: You can choose among the following topics: 1) Topic 1: Space weather missions and instruments design ESA is developing an enhanced Space Weather Sensor System to provide data for forecasting and to monitor Space Weather effects. Due to the to the asymmetry and complexity of Earth's magnetosphere, the involved particle environment and its dynamics, it is necessary to capture the state of the magnetic field and the particle distribution in a sufficiently large number of sampling points around the Earth, such that it allows state-monitoring and modelling of the involved processes with sufficient accuracy and timeliness. An important aspect for the realisation of observation systems for Space Safety is the need of high reliability, sufficiently long lifetime and low data latencies as the data will be used in operational purposes. For this, ESA is currently implementing and studying multiple dedicated Space Weather missions, from hosted payloads to nanosatellites and small satellites, that will be flying in a wide range of orbits. This will allow you to look into the different steps of an ESA space mission, from early study to mission implementation and management of flying missions. Your role would be to contribute to the mission development of upcoming missions, through analysis of the mission performance utilising different Space Weather models, instrument simulations and data, and mission analysis tools. These analyses will provide insight into the optimisation of the mission design and operations concept and will support the Space Weather team in guiding ongoing industry developments.
113.requirements: Topic 1: Knowledge and background in space/particle physics, simulations, and data science are assets. Previous demonstrated experience with programming is desirable. Topic 2: Background and demonstrated experience in UX, UI, HMI design and programming for software is essential Knowledge in designing ergonomic user interfaces and graphics is desirable

114.tasks: You will support the innovation team that is Spaceship EAC, working to further develop and advance the projects of the team. 1. Background and Motivation The Spaceship EAC team is always on the lookout for talented and motivated persons to join our projects and contribute to ESA’s exploration activities. The main areas in which the initiative is currently active are: energy production and storage; radiation shielding; In Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU); VR/AR technologies for exploration; embedded systems and IoT; exercise hardware and countermeasure concepts; machine learning for exploration; robotics and human factors; conceptual illustration/design. 2. Objectives As a member of the team, you will be asked to work on a project relevant to the topical areas aforementioned, advancing the project with the team and contributing to the overall Spaceship EAC environment. 3. Methodology and Tasks The internship will integrate into the existing Spaceship EAC/LUNA team at ESA and work on a specific project in the domains listed. The Spaceship approach relies heavily on practical engineering and proof-of-concept demonstration, adopting an agile, skunkworks-type mindset to our work. The project will demand a high degree of flexibility and creativity, in line with the innovation focus of Spaceship work. 4. Expected Outcomes You will help advance a specific Spaceship EAC project as well as become involved in the larger team. You will provide the technical outputs, prototypes and relevant documentation as a final deliverable to the team. 5. Relevance Spaceships exist as part of the ExPeRT team and are integral in early-stage practical demonstration of low-TRL technologies and concepts. These projects are then commonly advanced to higher TRL activities via other mechanisms within ESA or externally (e.g. in cooperation with research teams). Additionally, Spaceship projects can directly support activities at their home centre, e.g. EAC at Cologne, enabling new capabilities at the centre. Spaceship activities align with the broad objectives of the E3P and are enabling elements for low-TRL activities within the programme.
114.requirements: Knowledge and background in mechanical engineering, materials, computer science, life science, VR/AR development, industrial design or other relevant backgrounds are welcome.

115.tasks: You can choose among the following topics: 1) Topic 1: Robotics Our Spaceship team is always on the lookout for talented and motivated persons to join our projects and contribute to ESA’s exploration activities. The main areas in which the initiative is currently active are remote manipulation, embedded systems and machine learning. 2) Topic 2: VR/XR Our Spaceship team is always on the lookout for talented and motivated persons to join our projects and contribute to ESA’s exploration activities. The main areas in which the initiative is currently active are virtual and augmented reality applied to training, graphic design, human-machine interfaces & robotics. 3) Topic 3: Human Factors Our Spaceship team is always on the lookout for talented and motivated persons to join our projects and contribute to ESA’s exploration activities. The main areas in which the initiative is currently active are decision making and outreach with a focus on embedded systems, graphic design and human-machine interfaces.
115.requirements: A background in robotics, computer science, electrical/electronic engineering, mechatronics, aerospace engineering or a related field (Topic 1), together with an interest in virtual and augmented reality, simulation, visualisation (Topic 2) and human–machine interfaces (Topic 3), would be an asset. Familiarity with tools such as ROS/ROS 2, Unreal Engine or Simulink, and an interest in their application to space exploration and planetary surface operations, would also be advantageous.

116.tasks: You will contribute to the development and analysis of advanced structural solutions for space systems. The internship will focus on applying modern design, simulation, and testing methods to improve the performance, reliability, and efficiency of spacecraft structures. Depending on your background and interests, you may work in one of several key domains, such as: structural optimisation: exploring lightweight and high-performance structural concepts through numerical and computational design methods; fracture control and damage tolerance: supporting studies and simulations related to material strength, crack propagation, and structural integrity in extreme environments; vibro-acoustics: analysing vibration and acoustic environments during launch and their influence on structural behaviour; ultra-stable structures: investigating thermo-elastic stability and precision design techniques for optical or scientific payloads; hypervelocity impacts: studying the effects of micrometeoroid and debris impacts on spacecraft structures and assessing protection or resilience strategies through modelling and test data. You will learn how advanced structural engineering is applied to real space missions, gaining hands-on experience with modelling tools, simulation techniques, and engineering processes. Throughout the internship, you will be supported by experienced mentors who will help you connect theoretical knowledge with practical challenges in spacecraft design and verification. Learning outcomes include developing a system-level understanding of spacecraft structures, applying modern analytical and computational methods, and strengthening problem-solving and communication skills in a multidisciplinary engineering environment.
116.requirements: Knowledge and background should be in the field of mechanical/aeronautical engineering. Experience with relevant engineering software tools would be an asset.

117.tasks: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming Earth Observation (EO) by enabling the extraction of actionable insights from vast and complex datasets. ESA’s Φ-lab is at the forefront of this transformation through its active exploration of cutting-edge AI4EO technologies, spanning application-specific AI models, generative models, foundation models, and autonomous AI agents, with applications ranging from ground-based analytics to onboard satellite payload data processing (i.e., edge computing). You can choose among the following topics: 1) Topic 1: AI for Earth Observation As part of this internship, you will actively engage with Φ-lab researchers, staff, and Visiting Researchers and support a set of Φ-lab AI4EO research activities, including Geospatial Foundation Models (GFMs) for EO. You’ll gain hands-on experience across a number of steps of the AI development cycle: from EO data preparation and model training to benchmarking and testing of developed models. Tasks may include: preparing EO datasets for AI pipelines; training and benchmarking AI models for EO applications; supporting AI design and optimisation; supporting the ideation, preparation, and hosting of Φ-lab Challenges related to AI4EO. 2) Topic 2: Agentic AI for Earth Observation As part of this internship, you will develop and evaluate agentic AI for Earth Observation, contributing to research on how agents discover and access EO resources, plan and execute multi-step workflows, interact with external tools, and produce results that are scientifically grounded. Tasks may include: designing agentic workflows that decompose high-level EO objectives into sequences of analysis and processing steps; integrating EO tools and data services into agentic systems — data discovery, retrieval, processing, and interaction with specialised models; investigating reasoning, planning, and tool-use strategies that let agents adapt workflows to intermediate results and resource availability; building and testing prototype EO assistants, combining language models, geospatial foundation models, scientific models, and external tools as needed; benchmarking agentic systems on task completion, tool selection, reliability, efficiency, robustness, and scientific correctness; contributing to analysis, technical documentation, and scientific dissemination of results. You will gain hands-on experience in agent design, tool integration, scientific workflow automation, and evaluation for geospatial applications — and develop a working understanding of what it takes to make autonomous AI systems reliable, transparent, and scientifically trustworthy in Earth Observation.
117.requirements: The following elements are considered an asset: background in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Remote Sensing or related fields; knowledge and previous experience in AI4EO and EO data processing. Familiarity with the following would be appreciated: knowledge of agentic AI concepts with an interest in their application to Earth Observation; foundation Models for EO (Geospatial Foundation Models - GFM); Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR); previous participation in scientific challenges related to AI or AI4EO; knowledge of Edge computing or other disruptive computing paradigms for EO.

118.tasks: As an ESA Intern, you will contribute to the early validation of data products generated by FLEX, a new Earth Explorer satellite mission focused on monitoring photosynthesis and vegetation health. Your activities will span across the early operational phase of the mission, allowing you to contribute to the mission's scientific success from the very onset. Your responsibilities will include analysing selected satellite products acquired during the FLEX commissioning and early operational phases, investigating potential anomalies, and supporting the benchmarking of retrieval and validation methods. Depending on the progress of the mission and the specific activities ongoing during the internship, you may also contribute to the comparison of satellite products with reference and in-situ measurements. You will document your analyses and communicate the results to scientific and technical audiences, contributing to the assessment and progressive improvement of the mission’s products. Throughout your internship, you will gain practical experience in satellite data processing and validation, working with diverse datasets and collaborating in an international research environment. You will develop skills in data analysis, scientific communication, and project coordination, preparing you for a future career in Earth observation.
118.requirements: Sound scientific knowledge of remote sensing principles and applications is required. Demonstrated experience in using Python and C++ is an asset.

119.tasks: Harmony is ESA’s 10th Earth Explorer mission dedicated to the observation and quantification of small-scale motion and deformation (velocity gradient) fields to allow data-driven representations of processes in Earth System models, primarily, at the air-sea interface, of the solid Earth, and in the cryosphere. Due to the multi-faceted mission, a number of different simulation and performance estimation models have been constructed. The European Space Agency (ESA) is seeking a talented and enthusiastic intern to join our team to use and potentially further enhance the currently available mission performance evaluation tools. Key Responsibilities: use high-fidelity simulation environments to demonstrate the mission’s capability to deliver science data within the stated mission requirements; identify and suggest areas of improvement within the existing tools, both on fundamental aspects and on user-friendliness; use derived performance evaluations to construct, assess and quantify science data (Level-2) error budgets with a view to product validation metrics. Information on the Harmony mission can be retrieved here: EE10_Harmony_Report-for-Selection_21June2022.pdf.
119.requirements: You should also have: a solid understanding of and background in at least one of the Harmony science disciplines and applications; demonstrable programming skills with Python; knowledge of either active microwave (e.g. SAR) or optical remote sensing is considered an asset.

120.tasks: ROSE-L (Radar Observing System over Europe in L-band) is a Copernicus Expansion SAR mission that will provide L-band radar imaging of Europe, the global landmass, ice, and oceans. The uniqueness of ROSE-L is linked to the L-band wavelength, that penetrates deeper into natural materials like vegetation, dry snow, and ice compared to C-band, and enhances robustness for interferometric applications in scenarios with abrupt and large surface and ice motion. By coordinating data collection with Sentinel-1 operating at C-band, ROSE-L will maximise the benefits for users providing complementary information, more frequent radar images, and improved coverage across Europe and globally. The expanding availability of L-band satellite observations from missions such as the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar mission (NISAR), the JAXA ALOS-2 mission and the CONAE SAOCOM mission, together with dedicated airborne campaigns such as AGRIROSE-L and AfriSAR-2, provides a unique opportunity to support and shape future ROSE-L science activities through the analysis of real datasets. The European Space Agency is seeking a motivated and enthusiastic intern to support the assessment of the sensitivity and added value of L-band radar observations for selected applications. During your internship you will: identify, collect and process datasets from existing L-band SAR satellite missions and/or airborne campaigns such as AgriROSEL using established tools; transform the SAR image data into information such as soil moisture, land cover, forest biomass and other geophysical products for selected application areas, and assess the quality of the information through comparison with independent measurements e.g. field measurements; investigate the unique capabilities of L-band observations and their complementarity with other radar missions, with particular emphasis on the Sentinel-1 mission; document the datasets, methods, assumptions and analysis results in a clear, traceable and reproducible manner. Learning objectives By the end of the internship, you will have developed practical experience in: understanding how future Earth Observation missions are scientifically prepared, assessed and validated within ESA; processing and analysing spaceborne and airborne radar imagery; understanding how radar measurements contribute to higher-level geophysical products; communicating technical results through documented and reproducible analyses. More information on the ROSE-L mission can be found here: Copernicus L-band SAR Mission Requirements Document.
120.requirements: You should also have: solid understanding of at least one Earth observation application relevant to ROSE-L; demonstrable programming skills in Python; experience in processing and analysing satellite imagery. Knowledge of Synthetic Aperture Radar principles, microwave remote sensing, or geospatial data analysis would be considered an asset.

121.tasks: You will develop innovative technical Earth Observation scenarios and apply or develop relevant simulation tools to analyse the effectiveness of the use of Earth Observation satellite systems in synergy. The analysis will identify gaps in capability and explore opportunities for new systems of systems architectures and Earth system observatory concepts considering evolving European user needs in a holistic manner. Analyses will cover the 2024 – 2040 and 2040 – 2060 time horizons. Initial scenarios are to be built around mandatory core missions with reference quality performances (e.g. large Copernicus missions) complemented by other elements in a mixed system architecture approach. Potential tools / guidelines include initial EO system scenarios, an internal data base as well as complementary approaches to benchmark system design and compare different scenarios. These activities offer ample scope for the successful candidate to develop a detailed understanding of future EO space system architecture development using a system analysis-scenario based approach.
121.requirements: You should also have: knowledge of Earth Observation remote sensing technologies and the respective downstream science and applications; knowledge of relevant strategic and technological trends and developments inside/outside the space EO domain; IT knowledge in the areas of data bases and programming (e.g. Python).

122.tasks: The EGNOS V3 System is composed of 39 Remote reference stations, 2 Main Control Centres (hosting in particular the central processing facilities) and 6 Uplink Stations connected to 3 EGNOS geostationary satellites, all interconnected through a dedicated real-time wide-area network. EGNOS V3 design is the result of a complex multidisciplinary exercise implementing stringent performance, safety, security and operability requirements across several interconnected subsystems. Based on this first EGNOS V3 version, an enhanced engineering approach is being implemented for the definition of EGNOS evolutions, typically including: enhanced modularity of the system design through a system-of-segments approach; parallel engineering of evolutions across different EGNOS system releases; multidisciplinary consolidation within and across segments; interactive incremental validation and report generation using AI. You will be integrated into the System Engineering Section of the EGNOS and SBAS Division and will interact closely with the Security Service. You will also interact with other teams/disciplines (Product and Safety, Development and IVQ, Operations). You will develop, integrate and validate an EGNOS Engineering ToolKit aimig at demonstrating and providing an initial engineering capability in an integrated and shared environment including: a requirements engineering COTS tool; a Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) COTS tool; upgrading Internal AI agents and tools from previous activities to provide engineering support capabilities exploiting the current document-centric engineering approach (engineering artefact consistency checks, cybersecurity analysis, vulnerability and security patch identification, etc.) and extending these capabilities to cover standard security inventories; import/export functionalities to interface with external stakeholders. To this goal, you will: consolidate the System Engineering Team and Security Team user needs; analyse available technical documentation and identify relevant information; select and justify the choice of OSS/COTS tools complementing the current selected System Engineering tools; design, develop, integrate and validate the EGNOS Engineering ToolKit; demonstrate the capability of the EGNOS Engineering ToolKit to conduct security and system engineering activities; document the user manual. At the end of the internship, you will have contributed to an AI-assisted proof of concept demonstrating the capability to support security and system engineering activities.
122.requirements: software engineering with AI Agent; cloud computing; system Engineering tools and processes.

123.tasks: Space Thermal Analysis and Verification, covering one or several of the activities below: Mechanical Systems Laboratory: Participation in the testing activities of the laboratory including evaluation of test data. Participate in the development and acceptance of new test facilities, e.g. thermal cycling, Coefficient of Thermal Expansion; Thermal Analysis methods: Research and development in the area of computational methods for space thermal analysis or multi-disciplinary analysis e.g.: a. methods and tools for exchange of thermal analysis data with other disciplines such as structures (e.g. development of SINAS); b. co-simulation of thermal analysis models with other domains such as power or fluidics; c. next generation methods for radiative, fluidic or thermal analysis. Analysis methods in support of testing activities: real time model correlation or identification of discrepancies between model and test data, analysis methods for new test instrumentation such as infra-red cameras, data fusion of thermal analysis and test data, modelling of gas convection for cleanroom testing; Thermal Analysis: Perform thermal analyses, including steady state/transient analyses of instrument and satellites following familiarisation with project requirements and Agency’s tools (ESATAN-TMS). This may also include in-flight correlation of thermal analysis models for ESA projects. This task is often carried out in collaboration with the Thermal Control Section (responsible for design aspects).

124.tasks: Space Thermal Control Engineering, covering one or several of the activities below: Thermal Design & Analysis: Perform thermal design and associated analysis, including steady state/transient analyses of instrument and satellites following familiarisation with project requirements and Agency’s tools (ESATAN-TMS). This may also include in-flight correlation of thermal analysis models for ESA projects; Cryogenics: Investigate cryogenic technologies (active and passive coolers) for applications in future ESA spacecraft and launchers; Heat Transfer & Heat Rejection: Investigate heat transport technologies such as capillary and mechanically pumped two-phase loops, single-phase loops, heat pipes for thermal control; Thermal Protection: Investigate thermal protection technologies (both re-usable and ablative) for on-going and future missions (e.g. planetary exploration and sample return missions) and re-usable launchers; Generic thermal control technologies: Investigate innovative and advanced technologies for the Thermal Control Subsystem e.g. tunable infrared emittance coatings with electrochromic-based solutions, phase-change materials, heat pumps, etc. Investigate specific thermal technologies for small satellites and CubeSats.

125.tasks: As an intern, you will support the work of the Language Services by carrying out the following tasks: translation – from English into French – of a wide variety of texts relating to the Agency’s activities and processes, with some emphasis on scientific and technical subjects but also including legal, financial and administrative matters; terminological research and extracting terminology from Agency documents and other reliable sources in French, German and English; maintaining and drafting terminology records for the ESA Termbase, the Agency’s multilingual terminology database covering most areas of ESA activity. In performing these tasks, you will make use of the tools and resources available to the team.
125.requirements: Due to the nature of this position, native proficiency in French and a thorough knowledge of English and German are required. Experience in translation work and knowledge of CAT tools and other language technologies is a pre-requisite.

126.tasks: The Martian subsurface is believed to contain significant reservoirs of water ice and volatile-rich phases such as carbon dioxide and methane hydrates. Understanding the formation, stability and dissociation of these reservoirs is important for planetary science and for future in-situ resource utilisation concepts. During the internship, you will contribute to the development of numerical models of coupled thermal and fluid processes governing hydrate formation and dissociation in the Martian subsurface, using the Delft Advanced Research Terra Simulator (DARTS) and supporting numerical tools. Your activities will be: review the current scientific literature on carbon dioxide and methane hydrates under Martian conditions; implement and adapt numerical models describing hydrate formation, dissociation and volatile transport in porous media; perform simulation campaigns to investigate the influence of temperature, pressure, soil properties and climate conditions on hydrate stability; analyse and interpret modelling results and compare them with existing studies and observational constraints; contribute to the preparation of technical reports and scientific presentations. Learning objectives Through this internship, you will gain practical experience in: numerical modelling of coupled thermo-hydraulic processes in planetary environments; thermodynamics, fluid transport and phase-change processes in porous media; scientific data analysis, interpretation and communication of results; conducting research within an international space science environment.
126.requirements: Knowledge and background in the following topics is an asset: strong knowledge and experience of modelling tool (Matlab, Python); knowledge of fluid dynamics and thermodynamics (energy, exergy, enthalpy).

127.tasks: Recent AI developments have primarily relied on large-scale GPU-based cloud infrastructures, but this approach faces challenges with latency, power consumption, and data privacy. To address these issues, there is an increasing shift toward edge AI. Upcoming ESA missions will require greater on-board autonomy, utilising smart sensors AI powered. However, SWaP constraints may require energy efficient solutions, particularly when deployed on rovers, probes, or landers. The proposed activity shall highlight how event-based processing, neuromorphic technology, could effectively address these limitations, enabling efficient object detection, classification, and tracking. The proposed activity will identify use cases in which event-based, or neuromorphic, computing can outperform or complement artificial neural networks deployed on conventional FPGA, GPU, or TPU platforms. Key advantages include lower power consumption and reduced latency, particularly when event-based sensors, such as cameras, are paired with event processors. Whereas conventional frame cameras typically operate at 25–100 Hz, event-based cameras can achieve sampling rates of up to 1 MHz. Combining an event-based camera with an event processor can therefore significantly improve the tracking of fast-moving objects and operation in low-signal-to-noise conditions, such as low-light environments. Relevant datasets will then be identified or, if real data are unavailable, generated using a digital twin. This approach is particularly suitable for debris detection, landing, and proximity operations such as docking, servicing, and capture. Finally, a testbed based on Neuromorphyx boards will be deployed for laboratory demonstration. It will integrate a NeuroSight event-based camera (Prophesee GenX320) with a NeuroCore event inference engine (BrainChip AKD 1500). Neuromorphyx | Neuromorphic Edge AI Hardware
127.requirements: Knowledge and background in the following areas is an asset: AI knowledge; electronics.

128.tasks: Within the framework of the VEGA-E programme, the development of engineering tools is necessary to ensure continuous monitoring of the design loops of liquid rocket engines. The proposed internship is related to the development and validation of engineering models at both engine level (for the MR10 and MR60 engines) and stage level for the VEGA-E LPM (Liquid Propulsion Module). You will use state-of-the-art modelling tools to develop or extend the mathematical models of the aforementioned systems. These models will then be validated using available test results. The internship will include an initial training phase, during which you will be expected to become familiar with Liquid Rocket Engines (in particular MR10 and MR60) and propulsion systems (LPM), the modelling of their main elements using the EcosimPro software platform and the models already developed. The second part of the internship will be dedicated to the extension and validation of the dedicated engine and system models, using available experimental data. During the final phase, you will carry out data analysis and draft reports. During this activity, you will have the opportunity to collaborate closely with the IPT propulsion specialists and gain a broader understanding of the VEGA Space Transportation System.
128.requirements: Knowledge and background in Rocket Propulsion, Fluid Dynamics, Thermodynamics, and Heat Transfer are an asset. Due to the nature of the post, a commitment of six months is preferred, depending on the candidate’s availability.

129.tasks: You can choose among the following topics: 1) Topic 1: Mission-Agnostic Space Operations Visualisation Platform Modern mission operations require intuitive ways to explore and understand complex information. In this internship, you will help extend an existing visualisation tool with additional features and data integrations, to support mission planning, spacecraft monitoring, and training activities. You will contribute to the development of an advanced 3D visualisation platform for space missions operations. This includes displaying spacecraft trajectories, communication networks, events, and operational annotations in a clear and engaging way. Throughout this internship, you will gain experience in: developing interactive 3D and virtual reality applications; integrating and visualising operational data from different sources; designing features that improve situational awareness and decision making; working with modern game engines, such as Godot.
129.requirements: For Topic 1, experience with 3D graphics or visualization software (i.e., game engines, such as Godot, Unreal Engine, or Unity) is an asset. For Topic 2, the ability to communicate complex topics to diverse audiences through presentations, web content, and other communication materials is an asset.

130.tasks: FORUM is the Far-infrared, Outgoing Radiation Understanding and Monitoring mission, a research mission of the Earth Observation Directorate. It will be the first mission to take global measurements of Earth’s outgoing spectrum in the far-infrared at unprecedented resolution. These data will be used to investigate climate feedback from water vapour and clouds and ultimately improve climate models. FORUM will embark two payloads; The FORUM Sounding Imager (FSI) which is a Fourier Transform Interferometer working in the 100 to 1600 cm-1 spectral region and the FORUM embedded Imager (FEI). ESA - FORUM The Wave Interaction and Propagation Section provides expert support to the FORUM project on aspects related to instruments performances, Level 1 (from raw data to calibrated signal) and Level 2 (from calibrated signals to geophysical parameters) processors development, and mission performances evaluation. In this position you will be involved in FORUM performance assessment activities: ingesting the outcome of the on-ground characterisation tests of the instrument as parametrisation of the FORUM end-to-end simulator, to assess expected performances of the mission. You will run several sensitivity studies as a function of geophysical scene, or settings of the ground processing algorithms, to assess the impact on the Level 1 products (calibrated signals); using the FORUM end-to-end simulator, you will generate reference datasets to support: (a) the assessment of the performances at Level 2 (geophysical retrievals), (b) further scientific activities and (c) the development of the operational ground segment; you could be involved in the prototyping of calibration algorithms for FORUM.
130.requirements: Knowledge and background in optics (wave propagation and/or instrumentation) is an asset. Additional requirements: skills in numerical modelling and data analysis; experience in software development and coding in languages such as Python and Matlab (knowledge of C++ is an asset).

131.tasks: During your internship, you will be assigned to the Solar System & Exploration Missions Division which is responsible for operating the spacecraft of the Agency’s interplanetary fleet. Your assignment will focus primarily on the creation and extension of web-based operations tools which will support the flight control teams and spacecraft controllers in the execution of their daily work. In particular, you will design and develop backend functionalities for the retrieval, processing and generation of operational planning information and spacecraft configuration data as well as frontend features for appropriate visualisation and modification of said data. This will involve tasks such as: Assessment of relevant existing tools and functionalities within the division; collection of user requirements; devising a concept and software architecture to support the identified requirements; implementation and testing of the identified solution(s) .
131.requirements: Knowledge and experience in the following areas would be an asset: Python, Javascript or other programming languages; back-end development, e.g. Django; front-end development, e.g. Angular; Web Server Architecture; REST APIs.

132.tasks: You will support the XMM-Newton and INTEGRAL Flight Control Team to execute the mission operations and to assess the performance of the missions and their ground segment. You will build up experience in the following areas: General insight in the know how, organization and culture of satellite operations; Systems that measure the performance of the various ground segment and spacecraft elements. Specifically, you will have the opportunity to contribute to the development of a Ground and Space Segment Awareness System. This activity will also involve interaction with a European Graduate Trainee at ESOC. The exact tasks will be tailored to your skills, interests, and project needs. Through this assignment, you will gain valuable knowledge and hands-on experience in the design, functionality, and operations of a satellite control centre, with a particular focus on monitoring and visualising ground segment status. The Ground and Space Segment Awareness System provides a real-time overview of the spacecraft, ground segment and mission status, helping engineers understand what is happening across the mission. It enables them to maintain situational awareness, assess mission status and support investigating operational anomalies. The system should be updated and enhanced with new capabilities. Planned developments include the integration of spacecraft orbit visualisation with information on the Earth's radiation environment and improvements to the user interface and experience. Additional activities may include the implementation of further operational and user-driven requirements, such as enhanced visualisation of attitude and orbit control information. Depending on your interests and the project priorities at the time, there will also be opportunities to contribute to other system enhancements and operational support tools. This assignment provides exposure to both operational and engineering aspects of mission support systems and offers experience in a multidisciplinary environment closely linked to spacecraft operations at ESOC.
132.requirements: What you bring: Good programming skills in Python and familiarity with web technologies (JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, CSS); interest in developing practical software for data processing, visualisation and operational awareness; curiosity about satellite operations, space systems and ground-segment engineering; motivation to write clear, maintainable and well-documented code; a collaborative mindset and readiness to develop solutions iteratively based on operational needs and user feedback; experience with dashboards, data visualisation, Grafana or CesiumJS would be an asset.

133.tasks: You will work directly with a Meta Quest 3 and support the development of new concepts in using such headsets onboard the International Space Station. Your activities will include: combining immersive application development with machine learning methods to explore new capabilities for onboard assistance, interaction, data interpretation, and experimental operational concepts; helping to design, prototype, implement, and evaluate software components in close collaboration with the team; developing on-device real-time interaction features, sensor or data processing pipelines, computer vision-based functions, or software tooling depending on project needs; contributing to technical trade-offs, implementation work, and iterative testing of candidate solutions in a demanding applied environment. Your learning objectives are: obtain a high-level understanding of Human Spaceflight in Europe; gain experience in extended reality development; understand how applied machine learning methods can support operational use cases such as assistance, interaction, perception, and data interpretation; develop practical experience in designing, prototyping, and testing software components within a multidisciplinary engineering team; learn how immersive technologies must be adapted, validated, and matured for use in constrained and safety-relevant environments.
133.requirements: Essential Skills: proven experience in Unreal Engine development; intermediate C++ and/or intermediate Python proficiency; interest in extended reality development and machine learning applications; familiarity with version control and collaborative software engineering practices. Desirable Skills: knowledge of computer vision, Bayesian theory, or signal processing; experience with the ESA XR Plugin; experience with prototyping, experimentation, or technical evaluation of interactive systems; experience with popular machine learning computer vision models and/or software.

134.tasks: The traffic in valuable Earth orbits is expected to continue increasing significantly in the coming decades. Despite internationally recognised space debris mitigation guidelines, technical standards and national regulations, the successful disposal of space systems and the prevention of in-orbit break-ups remain major challenges. ESA is addressing these challenges through the implementation of the Zero Debris approach, helping to preserve the space environment for future generations. You will support the team responsible for further developing the Zero Debris approach and improving the End-of-Life management of current and future missions. Activities may include contributing to engineering studies, requirements, methodologies, technology roadmaps and analyses related to space debris mitigation, disposal strategies and the implementation of Zero Debris objectives across ESA projects. While the primary focus of the internship will be on Zero Debris and End-of-Life management, opportunities may also arise to contribute to activities in the areas of Ecodesign and In-Orbit Servicing and Circular Economy in Space, depending on the intern's interests and the needs of other ongoing activities.
134.requirements: Having a keen interest in Clean Space activities is beneficial and having a collaborative team spirit is highly valued. Knowledge and background in Zero Debris, space debris mitigation and/or space system engineering is an asset. Due to the nature of the post, a commitment of six months is preferred, depending on the candidate’s availability.

135.tasks: Assessment of Societal Benefits of Exploration Science: You will support the Exploration Science Office, in close coordination with the HRE Strategy Office, in developing and applying a structured approach to identify and evaluate the societal benefits generated by ESA’s exploration science activities, from ground-based analogue studies to research performed on ground and suborbital platforms, the International Space Station and future Moon and Mars missions. Societal Impact Framework Development: You will review methodologies and frameworks used by space agencies, research funders, and international organisations to assess the societal, economic, technological, health, and educational returns of publicly funded research. Building on this benchmarking, you will help identify indicators and propose a structured methodology tailored to exploration science, covering benefits such as advances in human physiology and countermeasure development, contributions to terrestrial healthcare (e.g. ageing, rehabilitation, cardiovascular and musculoskeletal health), technology and knowledge transfer (e.g., innovative materials, robotics, sensor and monitoring technologies, data science and AI), industrial and economic spin-offs, and educational and inspirational outcomes. Impact Mapping and Case Study Compilation: Using this framework, you will identify and document concrete examples of societal benefit arising from past and ongoing exploration science studies, such as bed rest and dry immersion analogue research, research on suborbital platforms, and ISS-based investigations, just to name a few. Working with scientists across the Exploration Science Office and the HRE Strategy Office, you will trace research outcomes to real-world applications and compile these into case studies and a reference repository to support impact reporting, stakeholder communication, and the design of future research calls. This internship offers insight into science policy and impact evaluation within human space exploration, with practical experience in framework design, benefit-mapping methodologies, and stakeholder communication.
135.requirements: Background: A background in life sciences, physical sciences, health or biomedical sciences, economics, public policy, or science communication is essential, along with a strong interest in space research and its wider societal relevance. You should possess strong analytical and synthesis skills, excellent written and verbal communication abilities, and a motivation to contribute to the assessment and communication of research impact. The ability to work independently while maintaining coordination with a team is important. The internship is designed for students in their final or second-to-last year of university studies, ensuring they have a solid academic foundation relevant to the tasks involved. Experience: Prior experience in space research is not required. However, familiarity with impact assessment methodologies, research evaluation, socioeconomic analysis, or science communication is considered beneficial. Any relevant experience in structured research, literature reviews, policy analysis, or data synthesis will be advantageous. Given that the internship targets students, the focus is on providing hands-on experience and skills development, rather than requiring extensive professional background.

136.tasks: Background The Earth Observation domain is exceptionally relevant at this time, becoming determinant in the definition of earth models for the prediction of environmental changes and at the same time identification of factors that could reduce their impact. The science community is confronted with a challenge objective for which it is critical to provide all the necessary elements for effective research. The increased amount of information and data available is creating the need to follow closely and timely the scientific community and react promptly to incoming needs. A close monitoring of the services deployed in the Earth Observation Framework for the handling of the data management, namely generation, archival and dissemination, is the only means of following closely the user behaviour and come back with proper solutions. Applying modern technology, a service for the monitoring of all functions deployed, together with a set of timely populated dashboards and regular generation of reports allows for faster reaction to issue or demand changes. In this particular case, we are looking for a young expert that could support the validation, identify improvements and further evolution of the approach in the collection, management and visualisation of metrics derived from all the operational services. Objective Validate the platform under development for the monitoring and reporting of the Earth Observation Framework for Science missions. How Your interfaces are ESA employees and possibly the industrial engineering teams involved in the relevant projects. You will initially familiarise yourself with the context, including basic concepts of data management and discovery. You will participate in the design and deployment of the platform and its sub-components. Based on a defined set of use cases and scenarios, you will support the team in testing, debugging, and improving existing systems. If time allows, you will deepen in proposing additional mechanisms for collecting, aggregating, and analysing digital data to track system health, performance, and availability. You will assess the application in terms of user experience and determine possible improvements by consulting with stakeholders (operational team, management leaders, service managers). You will present findings and project results to team members, stakeholders, and leadership. You will produce a final report of the obtained results.
136.requirements: Knowledge and background in the following areas: good programming (e.g. scripting) skills and/or data management skills; knowledge of information management and its application for data analytics is an asset; familiarity with project/service management principles.

137.tasks: As an intern in the Cost Engineering section, you will be involved in the following activities: maintenance of the technical-economic database that constitutes the backbone of the cost modelling capabilities; maintenance and development of cost engineering tools and models; support to Cost Engineers in various studies, mostly those performed in the Concurrent Design Facility.
137.requirements: The following are assets for this internship: knowledge of cost estimating and cost modelling; knowledge and background in engineering, and specifically space system engineering; knowledge of project management and related financial areas; proficiency with office automation software and customisation (e.g. Microsoft SharePoint and Excel).

138.tasks: You will report to the Head of the ESTRACK Stations and Infrastructure Section in the Ground Facilities Operations Division. This Section is responsible for the maintenance and operational management of the ESA Tracking Network (ESTRACK). The ESA Link Budget Tool is the reference tool of the European Space Operations Centre for the characterisation of the radio-frequency communication link between spacecraft and ground antenna. You will contribute to the continuous development, support, and optimisation of the ESA Link Budget Tool in a collaborative, user-focused environment. This role will also focus on assessing the environmental impact of ground station operations in line with the ESA Green Agenda initiatives. You will focus particularly on analysing data in terms of carbon footprint and providing concrete metrics and insights to guide future actions. Key Responsibilities: Link Budget Tool: Expand the Link Budget Tool catalogue for Near-Earth missions and ground stations With the growing number and diversity of missions supported by ESA, you will contribute to expanding the Link Budget Tool’s mission and ground-station catalogues. You will have the opportunity to analyse new requirements, perform testing, and further enhance the tool’s capabilities to support the Agency’s evolving operational needs. Link Budget Tool: Analyse capacity and optimise ESTRACK scheduling You will contribute to analysing ground-station capacity and workload, helping to identify opportunities to improve the allocation and utilisation of ESTRACK resources across missions. You will support studies and development activities aimed at integrating the Link Budget Tool with the ground-station scheduling system, which allocates ESTRACK ground-station coverage to supported space missions. This activity will involve close interaction with ground-station and mission operations teams, providing a unique opportunity to understand and contribute to the end-to-end process of planning spacecraft communications. Green ESTRACK: Review and Assess Sustainability Measures at ESTRACK Ground Stations You will evaluate existing and future sustainability initiatives and operational activities at selected ESTRACK ground stations, assessing their documented environmental impact, energy consumption, and effects on local energy grids. You will analyse available data from past and ongoing measures to determine operational efficiency and alignment with ISO 50001 energy management standards. Green ESTRACK: Develop and Maintain Sustainability Metrics and Dashboards You will design and maintain metrics in alignment with recognised sustainability standards. These metrics will help track the effectiveness of initiatives and demonstrate the tangible benefits of adopting sustainable practices. You will present the results clearly for both internal use and external reporting, highlighting the positive environmental and operational impact.
138.requirements: You should have a keen interest in sustainability, strong analytical skills and the ability to collaborate across different technical and administrative teams. Basic knowledge of Python programming code; basic knowledge of atmospheric propagation; familiarity with sustainability principles, carbon accounting, or environmental standards like energy management/ISO 50001; proactive, able to multitask and have strong self-motivation; good communication skills for handling a broad range of interfaces and the ability to work as part of an interdisciplinary team.

139.tasks: You will be based at the European Space Operations Centre (ESOC): the main mission control centre for the European Space Agency (ESA). ESOC’s primary function is to operate unmanned spacecraft on behalf of ESA as well as launch and early orbit phases. ESOC plays a role of sole service provider and its resources are dedicated to mission operations. Two of the challenges the Office faces are supporting the innovation culture in a high reliability environment, and the capturing and dissemination of the vast amounts of knowledge collected as part of this work. You will enjoy supporting Innovation and Knowledge Management at ESOC, whose aims will be defined depending on the skill of the candidate.
139.requirements: Additional requirements: A STEM background is an asset. Knowledge Management experience is an asset. Due to the nature of the post, a commitment of six months is preferred, depending on the candidate’s availability.

140.tasks: You will support the ESA Innovation Services Section in developing digital tools for supporting the monitoring of innovation activities, and the innovation process itself. Following a requirement and feasibility assessment, you will select one or more projects, for the development and prototyping of the following tools: dashboard for monitoring technology transfer activities; tool for discovering existing knowledge and technologies to solve problems (e.g. lessons learnt from past R&D projects and analogous solutions to similar problems), leveraging existing databases and AI agentic capabilities. tool for expert forecasting on technical questions, to efficiently inject collective intelligence into the design process. Learning Objectives: apply your software engineering or data science skills to develop and refine tools supporting ESA’s innovation services; gain practical experience in translating conceptual frameworks into operational software; contribute to ESA’s efforts to provide technology intelligence and support technical innovation; develop skills in AI and agentic systems, RAG, semantic search, knowledge engineering, and the analysis of structured and unstructured data.
140.requirements: You are a technically capable and curious problem-solver, able to design and prototype digital tools. You should be familiar with AI techniques, software development, data visualisation, Microsoft digital tools and stakeholder-oriented innovation work. Useful competencies include knowledge, skills and/or experience with: AI and data science fundamentals, including GenAI, agents, RAG, Natural Language Processing (NLP), semantic search and embeddings; python, APIs, data processing, technical architecture and rapid proof-of-concepts; structured and unstructured data modelling, analysis, abstraction and cross-domain problem-solving; Microsoft Power Platform, dashboards, data visualisation and user-centered interfaces.

141.tasks: Space projects continue to rely heavily on document-based engineering practices. Requirements, architectural descriptions, risks, interfaces, verification activities and technical decisions are frequently distributed across multiple documents, making navigation, traceability and maintenance increasingly complex throughout the project lifecycle. The objective of this internship is to investigate how engineering knowledge can be managed as structured and interconnected information rather than exclusively through traditional document deliverables. The work will explore the concept of a knowledge-centric engineering environment capable of promoting a single source of truth while preserving engineering governance, review processes and traceability. Using the EOCognitiveLab mission concept as a reference case, you will: analyse the information flows and engineering artefacts typically produced during mission preparation and system engineering activities; identify and classify key engineering knowledge objects such as requirements, decisions, risks, interfaces, verification activities, stakeholders and deliverables; develop a lightweight engineering knowledge model describing relationships and dependencies between engineering artefacts; investigate how modern collaborative technologies such as SharePoint, Microsoft Lists, Power Automate, Power BI and artificial intelligence assistants can support engineering knowledge management; design and implement a prototype engineering knowledge portal demonstrating selected system engineering capabilities such as requirements traceability, review baselines, decision tracking and verification management; develop visualisation concepts allowing engineers to understand dependencies, impacts and relationships across a complex mission architecture; assess benefits, limitations and adoption challenges associated with knowledge-centric engineering approaches for future Earth observation programmes. By the end of the internship, you will have gained practical experience in system engineering, digital engineering methods, collaborative platforms, knowledge management, data visualisation and Earth observation mission preparation. The results of the work are expected to support future initiatives aimed at improving the efficiency, accessibility and consistency of engineering information across complex space projects.
141.requirements: Knowledge and background in one or more of the following areas is considered an asset: systems engineering and complex engineered systems; aerospace engineering or space systems engineering; information systems and knowledge management; computer science, software engineering or data engineering; business process modelling and workflow automation; database design and information modelling; web applications and collaborative platforms; data analytics and visualisation; artificial intelligence applications for engineering environments; Microsoft 365 technologies, including SharePoint, Microsoft Lists, Power Platform or similar environments. Additional desirable skills include: ability to analyse complex processes and convert them into structured information models; interest in digital transformation and engineering collaboration; familiarity with graph-based data models and traceability concepts; strong analytical and problem-solving skills; ability to work independently while interacting with multidisciplinary teams; good communication and technical writing skills in English.

142.tasks: You will support ESA’s effort to evolve and to utilise the LUNA Analog Facility together with DLR as project partner. 1. Background and Motivation The LUNA Analog Facility is the central hub for the preparation, validation and training for lunar surface activities and technologies. While focusing on operational concepts and mission simulations, it also allows for substantial technology testing, scientific investigations, optimisation of operational protocols and procedures, and much more. The LUNA facility has been inaugurated in September 2024 and is being used for various research and simulation activities of ESA, DLR and external partners. Those include suited activities with suit simulators and dedicated EVA tools, as well as robotic activities concerning mobility, imaging, localisation and communications. At the same time that utilisation is ramping up, the facility is still being evolved with additional capabilities to further enhance and increase the immersion and simulation quality. 2. Objectives This internship project aims to support ESA’s evolution and utilisation of the LUNA Analog Facility by: supporting the development and integration of new capabilities through the element engineering process from requirements engineering to system design, manufacturing, testing and verification, commissioning and operations; supporting the operations and utilisation of LUNA in campaign activities with internal and external partners. 3. Methodology and Tasks The internship will integrate into the existing Spaceship EAC/LUNA team at ESA and – based on interest and needs – support one or multiple of the development and utilisation activities below. Additional topics may also be identified throughout the internship period. refinement of the concept of operations of LUNA and its application for campaign utilisation; habitation systems development and their integration into mission simulations; analogue space suit evolution and operations, incl. tools development; robotic or autonomous systems developments to support LUNA utilisation; dust monitoring and mitigation strategies for LUNA operations and future Moon missions; integration of research and technologies related to in-situ resource utilisation with LUNA. 4. Expected Outcomes Based on the actual task assignments, the outcomes of the internship will include contributions to the LUNA operations and utilisation documentation as well as procedures and training manuals. You will be directly involved in the LUNA operations, work with actual hardware and interface with scientific investigations in LUNA which could lead to production or contributions to publications and conference presentations. 5. Relevance As ESA, NASA, and international partners plan sustainable human presence on the Moon, LUNA will be instrumental to prepare and bring together European expertise for lunar science, technology development, astronaut and operator training, and lunar mission operations.
142.requirements: Knowledge and background in analogue activities, operations and hardware testing is an asset.

143.tasks: Recently, the space sector has been evolving at a rapid pace. This change has mainly been triggered by the emergence of New Space actors from various parts of the world and an enormous rise of start-ups in the space economy. This new era has also seen the re-emergence of system concepts, such as constellations, and the adoption of advanced technologies, including new frequency bands, artificial intelligence, and autonomous collision avoidance. For commercial satellite applications, it is becoming increasingly challenging to keep track of and understand the underlying movements, initiatives, actors, and technology developments worldwide. In that context, ESA has been enhancing its Market and Business Intelligence (BI) activities, and intends to reinforce its toolset, infrastructure and data systems to respond to such dynamism and capitalise on state-of-the-art BI capabilities. The main priorities are: improving the dissemination and accessibility of information; enabling data integration from multiple sources; developing tools for interactive visual data analysis. As an intern, you will have the following tasks: contributing to the further development of Market and Business Intelligence capabilities; supporting the design and implementation of data integration solutions; applying these developments to the satellite communications domain; helping transform raw data into actionable insights for the industry.
143.requirements: Knowledge and background in python or data system architecture would also be an asset.

144.tasks: BepiColombo is set to arrive at Mercury in November 2026, with the start of its nominal science phase in April 2027 for several years to come. The mission will deliver an unprecedented wealth of scientific results, offering a unique opportunity to reshape how planetary science is shared with both the scientific community and the wider public. While ESA’s Science Communication Office will highlight major milestones and achievements, many of the mission’s rich and diverse results will require additional, creative approaches to fully reach their audiences. In a context where media landscapes and communication practices are rapidly evolving, there is a growing need to explore new formats, platforms, and strategies to effectively reach and engage the right audiences. We are looking for a motivated and imaginative intern to help develop and implement innovative ways of communicating BepiColombo’s science results and key milestones, complementing ESA’s core communication activities. The role will encourage fresh ideas and new formats to enhance the visibility and impact of the mission’s discoveries. This may include crafting engaging scientific stories, contributing to the preparation and visibility of data releases, designing visual materials such as posters and infographics, developing scientific visualisations, and exploring novel formats such as data sonification, alongside proposing new concepts for outreach and dissemination. This internship offers a unique opportunity to experiment with new, creative, and transformative approaches to science communication at a pivotal moment for the BepiColombo mission.
144.requirements: You should also have: broad knowledge of science, with the ability to quickly understand and engage with new scientific concepts (knowledge of planetary science is an asset); strong interest in science communication, with the ability to translate complex scientific results into clear, engaging, and accessible content for different audiences; experience in at least one of the following areas is required: science writing, visualisation, or multimedia content creation. Depending on the profile, the internship will focus on developing innovative applications of these skills rather than basic training; creativity and curiosity to explore new communication formats and approaches, including emerging media, interactive content, or unconventional storytelling techniques (e.g. data visualisation, sonification, digital storytelling); awareness of evolving media landscapes and interest in identifying effective ways to reach and engage different target audiences across platforms.

145.tasks: In the context of elaborating and implementing the Agency's industrial policy it is important for ESA to maintain an in-depth understanding of the space industry and its characteristics. The focus of the here concerned activity is to contribute to the characterisation of the European space SME community. This concerns in particular statistical analyses of the economic and financial characteristics of European space SMEs and their involvement in the activities of ESA. To this end you will access a variety of available data sources of the Agency comprising programmatic, financial, and economic data (current and historic) concerning the European space industry working with ESA (note that access to the data and publication will be subject to a non-disclosure agreement). Your analyses will contribute to the extension and consolidation of the existing collection of data and models of relevant economic and financial characteristics of the space SME and Start-Up community. Your analyses will consist of performing in depth studies and statistical analysis that will consist of coding of related algorithms, machine learning and AI-based data exploitation as required. For the analyses you will be using a range of data sources of industrial policy relevance. The precise scope and content of the specific analyses to be performed during the period of the internship can be agreed with you in line with your research interests. You will be supported in your activities by the members of the SME Section and other services of the Department.
145.requirements: Knowledge of economics, statistics, econometrics. The activity requires the handling of large datasets. Proficiency with MS Excel is required and experience with data analysis software such as Python, Power BI, machine learning tools would be an asset.

146.tasks: Working with the Strategy team, you will help strengthen awareness of space exploration, ESA’s Human and Robotic Exploration programme and its benefits among decision-makers, space and non-space professional communities, and the public. You will contribute to: translating the directorate’s strategy and objectives into a coherent visual identity and brand; using the running and planned exploration missions (e.g. Astronaut missions, International Space Station, European Service Modules for Orion, Argonaut, Rosalind Franklin Mission) as a teaser to develop communication content to promote the exploration benefits and strategy narrative; initiatives to enlarge the evidence base of and communicate about exploration and socioeconomic, cooperation, political and science benefits; designing and implementing innovative ways to make the directorate’s activities more visible and accessible to the public and decision-makers; developing communication strategies, campaign concepts, plans, content and briefing materials; supporting the preparatory work to set up a communication strategy and plan for ESA's next Council meeting at Ministerial level, including defining objectives, key messages, target audiences and suitable channels.
146.requirements: Specific competence in one of the following disciplines is essential: Communication sciences, Science communication, Journalism and multimedia or similar.

147.tasks: During this internship, you will support activities aimed at improving the resilience of the supply of materials for the European space sector. You will investigate strategic raw materials, chemicals and advanced materials used in space applications and map their supply chains and key European and non-European dependencies. You will assess factors that could affect their future availability, including regulatory developments, industrial changes and geopolitical risks. You will contribute to identifying emerging vulnerabilities and possible measures to reduce supply risks and strengthen European capabilities. Through this work, you will learn how materials and space-specific manufacturing processes are used across the sector; how the complexity of industrial supply chains is assessed; and how regulatory, industrial and geopolitical developments can affect the availability of critical technologies. You will work closely with specialists in sustainable engineering, standardisation and chemicals regulation, and help translate your findings into improvements to internal materials and regulatory databases and tools. One of the objectives will be to develop a risk measurement approach to combine technology maturity, regulatory, geopolitical and potentially other relevant aspects.
147.requirements: Knowledge and background in European environmental and chemical regulations, software development, or material/chemical engineering is an asset.

148.tasks: You can choose among the following topics: 1) Topic 1: Process Automation and Digital Tools identify opportunities to automate repetitive or manual processes within market research, financial assessments, and application tracking; contribute to the design and development of simple internal tools (e.g., dashboards, templates, or scripts) to streamline data analysis and reporting; support integration and upkeep of document repositories, or shared databases used in engagement and tracking efforts; work with the team to pilot and evaluate automation tools to enhance operational efficiency. 2) Topic 2: Communication and Relationship with Industry provide hands-on support to companies during their application process, offering clear guidance and responsive assistance; collaborate with internal teams to create effective marketing materials, case studies, and outreach content tailored to different industry segments; assist in organising and supporting industry events, webinars, and matchmaking activities that foster ecosystem engagement. 3) Topic 3: Space Market Research and Business Analysis conduct research to identify and evaluate potential candidate companies within the space sector, supporting the development of a comprehensive and up-to-date ecosystem map; analyse business plans submitted by applicant companies, assessing their viability, innovation potential, and alignment with evolving space industry trends; support internal efforts to refine financial assessment processes, including data collection, scoring frameworks, and benchmarking practices; monitor and report on emerging industry trends, contributing insights for future thematic programme campaigns and strategic focus areas.
148.requirements: You are proactive and autonomous with strong analytical and organisational skills. You are able to identify inefficiencies and propose automation solutions within existing workflows using Microsoft-based platforms. You have knowledge of the financial ecosystem and an understanding of the investment lifecycle of a company, as well as knowledge of the European space ecosystem and space economy. The following are considered assets: experience with Microsoft 365 tools, particularly advanced Excel functions and macros, Power BI and Power Automate for process optimisation and reporting; a demonstrated interest in space technologies and start-ups; practical experience gained in a space start-up; knowledge and background in economics, finance or business administration; knowledge and background in marketing and communication.

149.tasks: We are looking for talented, enthusiastic interns with great multimedia skills (video, graphics, design) to be involved in exciting projects in the Space Training Team. You might be involved in making videos that will be watched by astronauts on board the International Space Station (or even on Artemis Moon missions!) or preparing media for training material for astronauts and the ground-based communicators who support them. There is always a new challenge, and new opportunities. Are you ready for them? Your tasks might include filming astronauts and editing material for production of public outreach and space training videos, as well as developing assorted multimedia (eg. infographics, illustrations, animations) for use in videos, PowerPoint slides, E-Learning, posters and other purposes. For further information on this internship, please click here: ESA - Space training team – media production
149.requirements: Excellent spoken and written English (C1). An interest in human spaceflight would be an advantage but is not essential as you will develop this! A scientific background or interest in science is advantageous but not a requirement as we will help you. Above all you must be enthusiastic, flexible and self-motivated. Essential skills: proficient in using Adobe CC (especially Premiere) or equivalent; good camera skills (Photo and video); good general multimedia/design skills. Helpful: experience in creating infographics and/or working with technical/scientific information; experience of using Learning Management Systems (eg Moodle, Blackboard, Canvas); audio processing skills.

150.tasks: Your main task will be to support the preparation of the next Technology Strategy at Directorate Level: prepare supporting material (data tables, visuals, briefing notes) for TEC management in the context of strategy preparation discussions; collect, consolidate, and analyse quantitative and qualitative data from ESA’s technology programmes, Technology domains, and application domains; support the creation of guidelines and recommendations to harmonise the use of digital tools (SharePoint, Teams, and IT tools) across the TEC Directorate. You will belong to the Accelerate and Innovation team: supporting initiatives to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of technology R&D activities through digitalisation, process optimisation, automation and continuous improvement; ensuring the integration of data, knowledge and digital tools across technology strategy, roadmaps, R&D activities and reporting processes to support informed decision-making and organisational learning; exploring opportunities for process automation and digitalisation, including the use of AI, with a focus on management reporting and knowledge-sharing tools. At the end of the Internship, you will: gain hands-on experience in the analysis of a large-scale technology strategy, including the collection and synthesis of data across multiple programmes and domains; gain hands-on experience in harmonising digital management tools (SharePoint, Teams, dashboards, AI-based reporting) within a large international organisation; develop proficiency in structuring and managing technical repositories, including content migration and collaboration with the ESTEC/TEC Communication team; acquire skills in data visualisation and smart reporting; understand the role of digital tools in supporting strategic and operational decision-making; learn how to support high-level strategic activities, such as contributing to ESA’s Technology Strategy; build familiarity with knowledge management practices and the integration of automation and AI; gain experience in cross-directorate collaboration, working closely with both technical and communication teams across ESTEC and TEC.

151.tasks: As an intern, you will support the work of the Internal Communication Products and Channels Office by carrying out the following tasks: creating Shorts for the OneESA Experience Platform addressing the ESA workforce. Shorts are an engaging way to display video content, based on posts from a Media news channel. They are ideal for the Employee App, bringing a familiar social media-style experience to the platform; creating and maintaining a dedicated Media channel or News page for Shorts on the OneESA Intranet platform; supporting the production of podcasts, images and videos; contributing to organising events and town halls for the workforce.
151.requirements: Knowledge of corporate communication, in particular internal communication and video production is a plus.

152.tasks: During the period of internship you will be faced mainly with the following tasks: identify areas where AI can enhance the audit process; gathering requirements from various stakeholders to ensure AI solutions meet their needs; researching and evaluating AI tools suited for audit processes; select and propose the appropriate AI technology; propose and possibly execute a plan for AI implementation for auditing activities, considering the following: ensure data quality, consistency and accessibility for AI applications including review and sustainable maintenance; ensure AI applications comply with relevant ESA regulations and standards; implement and conduct a pilot project to test AI applications in real audit scenarios; monitoring and validating AI model performance and making necessary adjustments; propose policies and procedures, as well as training material for the team members; generate reports and present findings to management and stakeholders. Learning Objectives: introduction and implementation of AI in highly regulated teams and processes; AI implementation at the European Space Agency; Industrial Cost Auditing processes; the European Space Agency environment; international Teams and teamwork.
152.requirements: Knowledge and background in business economics or audit is an asset.

153.tasks: As an intern reporting directly to the Head of the Brand Engagement Office at the ESA Communication Department, you will play an active role in the office’s graphic design projects. As an intern, you will support the work of the Office by carrying out the following tasks: supporting the graphic and UX development of digital brand engagement products; supporting the launch of a new range of ESA merchandise through the ESA Shop, both in physical locations and online; creating graphics for merchandise and supporting their implementation and promotion; creating digital products combining graphic design, UX design and creative storytelling; collaborating with various teams to ensure all products adhere to ESA’s branding standards and are communicated clearly online.
153.requirements: Knowledge and background in graphic design, UX/UI design and tools such as Figma, and communication are an asset.

154.tasks: As an intern, you will be integrated in the Capability & Country Support Division and will participate in the following tasks: process automation in SharePoint using Power Automate, Power Apps, Python and HTML/CSS/JavaScript; web-based apps development using React; Linux for the virtual machines; financial data handling and Power BI dashboards development; creation of supporting tools and procedures for the team to function more efficiently.
