155.tasks: You will be requested to provide analysis of several procurement or contractual texts, including on ESA General Contractual Clauses and Conditions; i.e. legal analysis of ESA specific regimes (Intellectual Property Rights, disclosure, Personal Data Protection, liability, export control ...) and their implementation in ESA General Clauses and Conditions; with specific focus on differences between General Procurement contracts, Express Procurement contract and Manpower and Service contracts, in the frame of the Contracting Regulations. You will obtain hands-on procurement experience in the space sector, while getting used to ESA procurement process through involvement in practical procurement cases, under the supervision of Contracts Officers from the two Divisions.
155.requirements: Additional requirements: excellent communication skills, both verbal and written; ability to interact with multiple international actors and to work collaboratively in a team to achieve organisational goals; discretion and integrity. The following would be considered assets: knowledge and background in space domain/technology; a good knowledge of contract, procurement or international business law, intellectual property law; a background in law, economics.

156.tasks: How do we engage diverse audiences across Europe? How can we make the best use of digital platforms to share compelling stories about space? What types of outreach activities help bring these stories to life and connect with people? By joining the Communications team at ESA's European Space Operations Centre (ESOC), you will gain hands-on experience in digital communications and public outreach. Working alongside experienced professionals, you will develop your understanding of how international organisations create and deliver effective, integrated communication campaigns in a multilingual environment. Your tasks will include: exploring ways to make articles, information sheets, and other content more accessible and engaging for the public through ESA's new content management system; supporting fact-checking and research activities; reviewing translated content; contributing to the creation and distribution of digital and audiovisual materials. Depending on your interests and skills, additional tasks may include: supporting new outreach initiatives; contributing to the development of audiovisual communication products for international audiences.
156.requirements: Due to the nature of this position, native-level proficiency in German is mandatory. Knowledge of Polish and/or Czech language is an asset.

157.tasks: You will put into practice the knowledge acquired during your studies, while supporting the activities of the DG Support and Members States Relations Section within the Director General’s Cabinet. The main tasks will be, in coordination with the other interns in the team, to support the daily tasks of the team and in particular: continuous monitoring of space activities and trends, political developments, and policy-related topics of selected ESA Member States; contributing to the weekly updating and distribution of the Member States observatory and associated products; supporting the preparation of background input for meetings of the Director General with ESA Member States; supporting the preparation of presentation material for engagements of the Director General; ad-hoc tasks in support of the team’s activities.
157.requirements: Knowledge and background in the areas of political or social science, international relations, space law, policy, politics, and/or related fields would be an asset.

158.tasks: As an intern, you will be involved in the following activities: analysis of the ESA Contracting Regulations and ESA’s unique rules and context; analysis of the ESA procurement rules as adapted for activities funded by the EU; analysis of the ESA General Clauses and Conditions for ESA Contracts; participation in the full procurement cycle starting from the preparation of tender packages, issue of the tender, evaluation of the proposals and placement of the Contracts. Through the participation in the above activities you will have a clear view of the main principles of public procurement applying to ESA procurements and at the same time you will have learnt the principles and international standards applicable to public procurement around the world which are mirrored in the ESA procurement rules.
158.requirements: Knowledge and background in Contract and European Law is an asset.

159.tasks: The European Space Agency (ESA) has a network of ESA Business Incubation Centres (ESA BICs) across Europe. Each year over 250 start-ups with a space-related business idea are selected for incubation, while over 2200 start-ups have been supported altogether. The ESA BICs help these start-ups to develop and grow their businesses. ESA routinely collects information about the incubatees and alumni of ESA BICs. This has been done to evaluate the socioeconomic impact of the ESA BIC supported start-ups in terms of revenue, employment and investments. As an intern, you will have the following tasks: process and analyse data from start-ups on a portfolio level; create and manage databases related to business incubation activities; identify opportunities for further automation of ESA BIC data collection, processing and visualisation, including developing new approaches and dashboards; prepare presentations and reports on findings; perform other assignments based on operational needs of the team, for example activity coordination, supporting on-site events, conducting business research.
159.requirements: Knowledge and skills in one or several of the following areas are required: statistics; data analysis; economic Key Performance Indicators for high-tech start-ups; MS Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint; statistical software (e.g. R, PowerBI); data automation and dashboards. The following are considered assets: programming languages (e.g. Python); experience with AI prompting.

160.tasks: During this internship, you will support the EBO Team with the following tasks: assist in monitoring of discussions, policy initiatives and legislative developments within European institutions; support the preparation of briefings, reports, presentations and background material related to institutional relations and cooperation with European institutions; contribute to the follow-up of legal and regulatory files, assessing their potential impact on space activities and programmes; participate in meetings, conferences and events, preparing summaries and identifying relevant outcomes and follow-up actions; collaborate with experts from different disciplines and gain insight into how policy, legal, institutional and programme-related activities support the development of the European space sector. Through this internship, you will develop a practical understanding of European institutional processes, space policy and governance frameworks, regulatory developments affecting the space sector and the implementation of major European space programmes. You will also strengthen your analytical, research, communication and stakeholder engagement skills in an international environment.
160.requirements: Knowledge and background in EU institutions and/or space policy is an asset.

161.tasks: You will support the Evaluation Office in conducting evaluations, organisational reviews and analytical studies aimed at improving organisational performance, efficiency and effectiveness. The team leverages a broad spectrum of analytical approaches, ranging from social science research methods to advanced data analytics and artificial intelligence to produce evidence-based recommendations. As a result, you will contribute to a diverse set of evaluation and analytics activities. Research and evaluation activities may include: conducting research, literature reviews and environmental scans; collecting, analysing and synthesising qualitative and quantitative information; supporting interviews and surveys; contributing to benchmarking studies; assisting in the preparation of analytical reports, presentations and management briefings. Data analytics and business intelligence activities may include: analysing administrative datasets; supporting data modelling and business intelligence; developing visualisations using Power BI; helping transform structured and unstructured data into actionable insights. This internship offers practical experience at the intersection of research, evaluation, data analytics and organisational transformation within an international public-sector environment.
161.requirements: A background in Economics, Statistics, Data Analytics, Business Administration, or a related quantitative or social science discipline would be an asset.

162.tasks: As an intern in the External Relations Department, you will have the unique opportunity to contribute directly to the management of the Agency’s relations with its international partners. This includes research on geopolitical and geostrategic developments of relevance to ESA and the space sector more broadly; foreign policy analysis; contribution to the formulation of internal positions and support to the implementation of ESA’s missions and programmes jointly carried out with international partners, in coordination with relevant programme directorates; and support to the handling of high-level meetings with international delegations. In doing so, you will be fully integrated into the team, contribute to the practice of international relations in a dynamic period of global change, and gain insights into the functioning of an intergovernmental organisation at the heart of the space sector.
162.requirements: Knowledge of the global space sector, relevant foreign policies or international relations is an asset.

163.tasks: Within the Education Office, you will build experience in inspiration activities for school-level children and families, and in outreach activities for the education programme, such as: support the creation and organisation of inspirational events and informal education resources; User Experience/Interface (UX/UI) and Publications: web front-end towards user experience optimisation, writing and publishing of articles, social media posts, video scripts; other school level STEM education related tasks. Learning areas: Web User experience (UX/UI), Informal STEM Education, Social media, Communication, event organisation.
163.requirements: Knowledge of and/or experience in any of the following areas is a major asset: STEM subject knowledge; communication, science communication; content management systems and social media; basic video editing; event organisation; knowledge and background in both English and French is an asset.

164.tasks: You will support the Institutional Law Division on legal matters relating to the governance and functioning of an international organisation. Topics may include: the institutional framework and decision-making procedures of the European Space Agency, including the work of its Council and subordinate bodies; the interpretation and application of the Agency’s internal rules, policies and legal instruments; legal questions concerning the status, privileges and immunities of an international organisation; the interaction between public international law, European Union law and the national laws of Member States; legal research, analysis and drafting in support of the Division’s advisory work. Through these activities, you will gain practical knowledge of institutional law and strengthen your legal research, analytical and drafting skills. As an intern, you will have the following tasks: carry out legal research and analysis on public international law, including European Union law, and the relevant national laws of the jurisdictions in which the Agency operates; prepare and contribute to the drafting, review and processing of a variety of legal instruments (agreements, memoranda, etc.) and other documents; monitor and review developments in international law, including the evolution of legal doctrine and its practical application in international organisations; contribute to the Department’s daily operations by supporting the work of legal officers.
164.requirements: Knowledge and background in public international law, including European Union law, and the relevant national laws of the jurisdictions in which the Agency operates, demonstrated through both study and experience, are an asset.

165.tasks: You will support the Intellectual Assets Strategic Management Office in the monitoring, administration, and utilisation of ESA patent assets and, where relevant, selected software assets. Your internship will focus on practical portfolio administration, licensing support, and the preparation of patent assets for commercialisation and technology transfer. As an intern, you will have the following tasks: supporting patent utilisation tracking by collecting, checking, and organising information on how selected patent assets are used in missions, research and development activities, licensing discussions, industrial products, services, or technology transfer cases; assisting with portfolio administration, including the preparation of short portfolio notes, status updates, and supporting material for internal review and decision-making; helping to prepare clear, non-confidential descriptions of selected patent assets for promotion to industry, including summaries of the technical problem addressed, the proposed solution, possible applications, and development status; supporting licensing and commercialisation activities by helping to organise information on potential users, interested companies, relevant technology domains, and follow-up actions under the supervision of the office; contributing to the review of selected software assets where they are connected to patent promotion, technology transfer, or commercialisation opportunities; interacting with ESA inventors and technical experts to clarify technical content and understand the maturity, possible uses, and exploitation potential of selected inventions; supporting coordination with ESA commercialisation stakeholders, including Business Incubation Centres, Technology Brokers, Phi-Labs, industry, and academia, where relevant to the promotion or use of patent and software assets; helping to maintain structured records, trackers, and short analytical summaries that support portfolio management, licensing follow-up, and reporting; supporting other related activities within the office, as required.
165.requirements: Knowledge and background in intellectual property or technology management is an asset.

166.tasks: You will support the Division of New Initiatives and Commercialisation in addressing legal matters arising in the preparation and implementation of ESA programmes and activities. Topics may include: legal questions linked to the commercialisation of space activities and the development of new services and business models, and innovative forms of cooperation with industry; programme-related matters, including the preparation and implementation of contractual and cooperation frameworks; issues relating to procurement, funding, intellectual property, data, liability, governance and the allocation of risks and responsibilities; interpretation and application of the Agency’s internal rules, policies and legal instruments; legal research, analysis and drafting in support of the Division’s advisory work. Through these activities, you will gain practical knowledge of institutional law and strengthen your legal research, analytical and drafting skills. As an intern, you will have the following tasks: carry out legal research and analysis on public international law, including ESA’s legal framework and European Union law, and the relevant national laws of the jurisdictions in which the Agency operates; prepare and contribute to the drafting, review and processing of a variety of legal instruments (agreements, memoranda, etc.) and other documents; monitor and review developments in international law, including the evolution of legal doctrine and its practical application in international organisations; contribute to the Department’s daily operations by supporting the work of legal officers.
166.requirements: Knowledge and background in public international law, including European Union law, and the relevant national laws of the jurisdictions in which the Agency operates, demonstrated through both study and experience, is an asset.

167.tasks: How do we engage diverse audiences across Europe? How can we make the best use of digital platforms to share compelling stories about space? What types of outreach activities help bring these stories to life and connect with people? By joining the Communications team at ESA's Establishment in Italy (ESRIN), you will gain hands-on experience in digital communications and public outreach. Working alongside experienced professionals, you will develop your understanding of how international organisations create and deliver effective, integrated communication campaigns in a multilingual environment. Your main tasks will include: supporting, in close collaboration with the Public Relations team, the organisation of the School Days taking place in March and April and the organisation of the ESA Open Day, taking place at the end of September. Additional tasks will include: assisting with organisational and logistical activities; drafting communications articles in English and Italian about PR events taking place at ESRIN; identifying and contacting event stakeholders; liaising with colleagues and other stakeholders within the Communication Department.
167.requirements: Due to the nature of this position, native-level proficiency in italian is mandatory.

168.tasks: The ESTEC/TEC Communications Team at the European Space Agency (ESA) in Noordwijk, the Netherlands, is offering a six-month internship focused on visual communication, graphic design, presentations, and communication support for events and outreach activities for the Technology Programmes. This internship provides an opportunity to learn about and contribute to the communication activities of ESA's technical directorate through visual storytelling, design, presentations, and stakeholder engagement. Visual Communication & Graphic Design: learn about ESA's branding guidelines and visual identity; assist in the creation and adaptation of communication materials for digital platforms, reports, exhibitions, and events in order to communicate the key messages of the Technology Programmes; support the development of graphics that help communicate ESA technologies, projects, and activities. Infographics & Presentation Design: gain experience in creating and updating infographics that communicate complex technical information in a clear and engaging way; assist in the preparation of presentations using Microsoft PowerPoint and other design tools; learn how visual storytelling supports effective communication with diverse audiences. Event & Communication Support: support communication activities related to events, workshops, visits, and outreach initiatives; assist with communication materials, participant information, and visitor engagement activities; gain insight into how communications and events contribute to stakeholder engagement within ESA. Further Opportunities Within the Team: participate in editorial, multimedia, and digital communication activities; collaborate with colleagues from across ESA's technical and communication communities; contribute to projects that showcase ESA's technologies, missions, and people. By the end of the internship, you will: gain practical experience in applying ESA branding and communication standards in collaboration with Corporate Communication; develop skills in graphic design, infographic creation, and presentation development; understand how visual communication supports a large international technical organisation; gain exposure to events, outreach activities, and stakeholder engagement; experience working within a multidisciplinary communications team in an international environment.

169.tasks: During your internship, you will support the day-to-day facility, workplace and site management activities at the European Astronaut Centre. Your responsibilities may include: supporting the coordination and follow-up of facility management services and service providers; assisting with workplace and accommodation management activities, including workplace allocation, occupancy planning and implementation measures; contributing to the coordination and monitoring of minor works, maintenance activities and site improvement projects; supporting the preparation and follow-up of meetings, action items, inspections and other operational site management activities; assisting in the collection, monitoring and analysis of workplace and facility management data; supporting communication and coordination with building users, service providers and other internal and external stakeholders; contributing to site development activities and continuous improvement initiatives aimed at enhancing the workplace environment and operational efficiency. Through this internship, you will gain practical experience in facility, workplace and site management within an international organisation. You will develop an understanding of how a complex operational site is managed, how diverse stakeholders are coordinated and how workplace needs are translated into effective and sustainable solutions. In addition, you will gain insight into the relationship between day-to-day operational activities and the planning and delivery of larger site development projects.
169.requirements: A background or academic knowledge in facility management, real estate management, architecture, civil engineering, industrial engineering, workplace management, or a related discipline would be considered an asset. Strong organisational and communication skills, combined with an interest in working in an international and operational environment, would be advantageous. Proficiency in standard office software applications, together with an interest in data analysis, digital workplace solutions and facility management technologies, would be beneficial.

170.tasks: You will support contracting activities for the Science Programme. You will help review procurement documentation and contractual provisions; analyse contractual, programmatic and procedural questions; compare approaches across different contract types; and contribute to active procurement cases under the supervision of a contracts officer, with due regard to operational and time-efficiency as well as continuous evolutions. By the end of the internship, you will understand the main stages of public procurement in the space sector, apply contractual and regulatory principles and collaborate effectively with technical, legal and programmatic stakeholders.
170.requirements: Priority will be given to candidates studying Law. Knowledge and background in space domain/technology is considered an asset. A good knowledge in contract, procurement or international business law, intellectual property law is considered an asset. Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written. Ability to interact with multiple international actors and to work collaboratively in a team to achieve organisational goals. Discretion and integrity.

171.tasks: You can choose between the following topics: 1) Topic 1: ESA Member States National security policy and capabilities’ review in support of DG-OS daily work as well as the EU security, defence and space evolution. Security from Space aims at defining space contributions to mitigate security challenges on Earth (the impact of Climate Change on land, sea and air and how this affects local populations including but not limited to human migration, human trafficking, illegal activities, border control, conflict areas, etc.). Space supports security crisis response. You will support the Office to: identify national policies of European states and their allies, the EU, as well as competitors regarding civil security/safety/protection; monitor existing national space capabilities and their link to security applications and if and how they can network together in support of the European Resilience from Space (ERS) programme. This entails the identification of capability gaps. And potential cooperation (Pooling and Sharing). 2) Topic 2: Space systems and Dual-Use: the case for ESA and commercial companies. The commercial sector both in the US and in Europe is successfully developing solutions that were previously only pursued by government. This has led the US Space Force to work on fully integrating commercial solutions into the national security space architecture to maintain the US’s competitive advantage in the sector. You will support the Office in investigating key questions, such as: How could ESA contribute to creating European commercial space champions in support of European space security and defense for Europe to leverage the use of commercial space solutions in a new “hybrid” architecture? How could the US Space Force Commercial Space Strategy be translated into the European context?
171.requirements: Knowledge and background in Space Systems and European Defence current Architecture is an asset.

172.tasks: Through this internship, you will gain, particularly in the context of the automotive and micro-mobility sectors: a comprehensive overview of innovative services based on integrated space-based data and terrestrial technologies; an in depth understanding of future trends in the automotive industry and the emerging role of the space industry in the automotive value chain; experience in business development and an understanding of business models. You will aim to build a comprehensive understanding of the market opportunities in the mobility sector for downstream space applications to support the development of sustainable, green and innovative applications. The emphasis will be on the automotive and micro-mobility industries, where ESA has a number of working groups and initiatives with external partners. As an intern, you will have the following tasks: identifying and characterising commercial opportunities for innovative services and applications in the mobility sector exploiting space assets such as satellite communications, satellite navigation, and earth observation; supporting the identification of and engagement with champion industry stakeholders and public entities that may become potential customers and users of the mobility services identified; supporting the characterisation, documentation and organisation of relevant industrial contacts and stakeholders; identifying gaps in existing technologies and services and supporting the identification of new developments in both terrestrial and space-based technologies, including emerging technologies.
172.requirements: The following are considered assets: knowledge of the automotive sector; knowledge of business development and commercial topics; an interest in new and emerging technologies.

173.tasks: Within the Education Office, the intern will contribute to the design and development of innovative educational resources and online learning activities aimed at supporting teachers and educators in integrating STEM topics and space-related content into their teaching. Particular emphasis will be placed on learner-centered methodologies, digital tools, accessibility and the effective use of ESA’s space-related resources in educational contexts. Tasks will include: contributing to the creation of the new didactics activities and resources making use of space mission examples; contributing to the definition of learning objectives and e-learning products architecture; writing video message scripts, story boards, and developing physical video demonstrations; integrating e-learning content in the ESA Education LMS (Learning Management System); other STEM didactics-related tasks. Learning areas: school-level STEM education, technology applied to school-level education, inquiry-based/project-based didactics, Instructional Design, Learning Management Systems, e-learning content Authoring Tools.
173.requirements: Knowledge of and/or experience in any of the following areas is a major asset: STEM subject knowledge and/or STEM education/didactics and/or Instructional Design; basic knowledge and/or experience in e-learning systems (LMS) and or Content Management Systems (CMS); basic knowledge and/or experience in video/image processing; knowledge and background in both English and French is an asset.

174.tasks: Interns in the Strategy Department will contribute to the implementation of Strategy 2040, at the heart of ESA’s efforts to shape the future of Europe in space. Depending on their path, interns may support activities in Strategic Initiatives and Strategic Coordinations. You can choose among the following topics: 1) Topic 1: Strategic Initiatives (SLE-SC) Within the Strategic Initiatives Team, you will be involved in the practical activities behind new strategic initiatives, helping turn ideas, inputs and discussions into clear actions and useful material. You will support the preparation, coordination and follow-up of activities, helping the team organise information, prepare concise inputs for internal discussions, monitor ongoing work and keep workshops, Strategy Forums and competitive Innovation Sprints running smoothly. You will contribute to: exploring strategic themes, emerging trends and relevant space-sector activities, then turning your findings into clear and useful summaries; bringing structure to information on innovation-related activities, helping the team track progress, spot connections and prepare internal reporting; shaping practical material for meetings, workshops and management discussions, including briefing notes, slide decks and short summaries; keeping collaborative activities moving by consolidating inputs, updating trackers, preparing agendas, capturing key points and following up on agreed actions; helping develop new tools and dashboards that make activities easier to monitor, analyse and communicate; engaging with colleagues from different teams and, where relevant, external partners by preparing practical material and helping turn collaborative inputs into usable outputs; supporting the organisation of lively strategy and innovation events, such as strategy forums, innovation sprints and innovation-focused workshops; supporting communication activities by helping to develop clear messaging, simple visual material and short articles.
174.requirements: Strategic analysis and research interest in strategic planning, public policy or international affairs; knowledge of innovation management or a related field; ability to analyse and synthesise information from multiple source; good written and verbal English communication skills; ability to prepare clear and structured reports and presentations. Digital tools and data analysis interest in digital transformation and data-driven decision-making; knowledge of software development is an asset. Personal skills proactive attitude and willingness to learn; curiosity, initiative, and the ability to work both independently and as part of a multicultural team; strong organisational skills and attention to detail; ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines.

175.tasks: As a Contracts intern, you would have the opportunity to gain first-hand exposure to the legal and contractual challenges arising from innovative space projects, while developing an understanding of how legal expertise can contribute to the development, deployment and commercialisation of space technologies and applications. You would learn alongside contract officers and specialists from different nationalities and professional backgrounds, in a collaborative and international environment. This is an opportunity to combine your legal skills with an interest in cutting-edge space technology and to see how contracts and legal frameworks can help transform innovative ideas and space assets into real-world satellite applications. You will learn how procurements are performed at an international level, you will understand what the requirements to launch a public procurement are, what is the best procurement procedure for your objective, how to make sure that the procurement is performed according to the principle of fairness, ensuring equal treatment of the involved bidders and how to select the best offer with respect to the budget available. The experience you will gain may help you further to go on working in the legal practice as a lawyer or as legal counsel in a company dedicated to the booming space sector. During your internship, you will prepare contracts, adapting them to the objectives of the procurements.
175.requirements: Knowledge and background in mergers and acquisitions is an asset and so is the knowledge of AI. Knowledge of technology and law would also be an asset.
